scope: Offline independent audit of the terminated real-M1 attempt008 capture and archived runtime sources. This is a separate semantic evidence review, not a replacement or modification of the original strict classifier receipts. No source/capture edits, build, SSH, device access or goal API call; only this report is written.
capture_consistency: The final console, challenge input, before-start, original-observations and verified-inputs files are byte-identical to the previously supplied attempt-008-partial snapshot. Final console receipt independently matches the 23684-byte raw file and its SHA256; no reader error is recorded.

inspector.limit: The copied final directory contains helper and controller source snapshots, but no separate inspector snapshot. Inspector identity is corroborated by the recorded hash and unchanged locally retained reviewed bytes.

runtime_source_binding.future_head_excluded: Later command changes including stderr redirection were not used to judge attempt008. Its exact archived command and strict regex were reviewed.

checks: Independently ran the retained inspector's verify_manifest on the real candidate002 packet and contents.
Verified-inputs candidate artifact/pin maps equal original-observations packet artifact/pin maps and the actual packet verification result.
before-start image_sha256 equals the actual collection hash; payload RAMDisk SHA256 equals the packet ramdisk hash.
artifact_binding.prepared_image_limit: Prepared bytes were not regenerated in this audit; this hash agrees with the earlier root-owned pinned-Construct offline record.

target_binding.guest_policy: before-start declares the four-zero-byte guest kernel-ctrr-to-be-enabled property, with both CTRR/PPL protection claims false.
target_binding.scope: Observed target records from root's actual proxy session, independently checked offline. The experiment is XNU on the real M1 under m1n1 HV, not a bare-metal boot.

challenge_audit.exact_command_check: Input exactly matches the archived protocol: export PATH; printf BEGIN with two separate 24-hex nonce arguments; uname -s; uname -m; uname -r; printf END with those same separate arguments; final CR.
challenge_audit.echo_assessment: The console contains terminal cursor movement, wrapping and split-argument command echo. The saved input is the exact transmission record; the terminal-rendered echo is not byte-identical to it and was not used as response proof. The unique joined markers and uname answers appear only in the subsequent response block.
ordered_response: Joined DL9_BEGIN marker for the saved nonce
Two precise uname PID4 malloc postlude-guard warnings
Two precise uname PID5 malloc postlude-guard warnings
Two precise uname PID6 malloc postlude-guard warnings
Joined DL9_END marker for the same nonce
challenge_audit.intermediate_line_accounting: After accounting only for CR line endings, all six non-answer lines fully match the observed uname(pid,hex-address) malloc postlude-guard warning form. No unclassified line appears between the joined markers. Answers occur once each in command order.
challenge_audit.semantic_conclusion: The shell evaluated both split-literal printf commands, executed all three uname requests and returned to its prompt. Echo alone cannot explain the joined nonce markers absent from input or the separate Darwin/arm64/version answer lines.
challenge_audit.malloc_scope: Warnings did not prevent these three commands returning their answers. This does not qualify malloc guard correctness or establish a complete malloc root cause.

original_receipts_preserved.false_negative_reason: The archived regex requires BEGIN, Darwin, arm64, version and END on adjacent lines. Interleaved malloc diagnostics violate that adjacency although the command results are present. No diagnostic lines were removed from the stored console or original validator.

recovery_audit.reset_intent: attempt1, workers_stopped=true, acquisition_probes_stopped=true, external reboot serial command; guest completion receipts precede the recovery path in the archived controller.
recovery_audit.latch_limit: Root reports the incomplete-state latch absent. The archived controller appends LINUX_VERIFIED only after ops.clear returns; the copied result is consistent with that path. No standalone latch observation is included in this copied evidence, and this reviewer did not query the M5 filesystem.

limits: This is evidence of a real interactive Darwin shell and the tested uname commands under m1n1 HV, not qualification of a complete OS, bare-metal boot, production protections or drivers.
The original automated checker remains false and its worker/controller receipts remain intact; this report supplies a separately justified semantic conclusion.
No new hardware boot or protocol change is required to establish what the immutable attempt008 bytes already show. Later stderr-redirection changes need their own future evidence if exercised.
